description: Saved regional investigations from the official GISTEMP input, not live requests. Source and dates are included per entry.

provenance.citation: GISTEMP Team, 2026: GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP), version 4. NASA GISS. https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/ (accessed 2026-11-13). Lenssen et al. (2024), doi:10.1029/2023JD040179.
provenance.origin: direct HTTPS download from NASA GISS with TLS verification

variable.name: Surface temperature anomaly
variable.definition: GISTEMP v4 combines land-surface air and sea-surface water temperature anomalies relative to 1951–1980. Regional results average available grid-cell centers inside the selected box.

ols.notes: Standard parametric linear model. Assumes uncorrelated residuals.

theil_sen.notes: Median of pairwise slopes on elapsed time. Rank-based slope interval does not correct for serial dependence.

mann_kendall_original.notes: Standard non-parametric rank test for monotonic trends. Does not correct for serial autocorrelation.

mann_kendall_hamed_rao.notes: Modified rank correlation adjusting variance for serial autocorrelation. Recommended for geophysical time series.

seasonal_mann_kendall.notes: Evaluates monotonic trend across individual calendar months without requiring deseasonalization.

warnings: Regional box average, not an exact country-outline average. Cells are weighted by cos(latitude); at least 50% of selected cell weight must be available per month.
The Theil–Sen slope interval does not correct for serial dependence; it is distinct from the Hamed–Rao significance test.

summary.plain_language: Between 2001 and 2026, Surface temperature anomaly in this region had an estimated rate of +0.356 °C anomaly per decade; 95.0% Theil–Sen interval (serial dependence not corrected): [+0.042, +0.676] °C anomaly/decade. This trend is NOT statistically significant under Hamed-Rao Modified Mann-Kendall (p = 0.1237, alpha = 0.05). This does not establish that the region is unchanging.
